newsitem.title: UK: City of London to increase security - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: City of London to increase security - newspaper.

text.p: Authorities in the City of London plan to enlarge the protective ring around the financial district as police warn the threat of an IRA attack is still high, the Financial Times said on Wednesday.

The scheme would extend the traffic restrictions and security cordon first set up following an Irish Republican Army bomb attack in the heart of the financial "Square Mile" in February 1993, the newspaper said.
Councillors of the Corporation of London, responsible for running the area, are expected to approve the extension at a meeting on Thursday after 10 months of consultation.
"The risk that the City of London might be a target for the IRA remains high...and in the run up to Christmas, there is always special concern," a corporation spokesman said.

The IRA ended an 18-month truce in its 25-year war against British rule in Northern Ireland in February when it detonated a bomb in London's Canary Wharf business district, killing two and causing hundreds of millions of pounds in damage.
In June an IRA truck bomb devastated a shopping complex in Manchester city centre.
